questions.q: What is the main limitation of using PCIe for GPU-to-GPU communication during training?
options: PCIe does not support GPUs at all
PCIe is shared, general-purpose infrastructure that is dramatically slower than NVLink and often routes through the CPU
PCIe only works with a single GPU per server
PCIe cannot be used alongside NVLink in the same server
questions.explain: PCIe is the general-purpose bus connecting a GPU to the rest of the system. It's shared and, for GPU-to-GPU traffic, is far slower than NVLink and often has to route through the CPU's PCIe root complex.

questions.q: Roughly how much faster is NVLink 4 than a single PCIe Gen4 x16 link?
options: About 2x faster
About the same speed
More than 20x faster
NVLink is actually slower than PCIe
questions.explain: NVLink 4 provides around 900 GB/s of bidirectional bandwidth per GPU, versus roughly 32 GB/s for a PCIe Gen4 x16 link — more than a 20x difference.

questions.q: What does an NVSwitch provide in a multi-GPU server?
options: A backup power supply for the GPUs
A dedicated switch chip giving every GPU a direct, full-bandwidth path to every other GPU
A way to run multiple operating systems on one GPU
A cooling mechanism for NVLink cables
questions.explain: NVSwitch is a dedicated switch chip that gives every GPU in a server a direct, full-bandwidth connection to every other GPU, rather than an uneven point-to-point mesh.

questions.q: In the output of `nvidia-smi topo -m`, what does "NV12" between two GPUs indicate?
options: The GPUs are not connected at all
The GPUs are connected via an NVLink path
The GPUs are connected only through system RAM
The GPUs are on different physical servers
questions.explain: An "NV" entry in the nvidia-smi topo -m output indicates an NVLink connection between that pair of GPUs, as opposed to "PHB" which would indicate a path through the PCIe host bridge.

questions.q: Why does interconnect topology matter for multi-GPU training performance?
options: It only affects how the server looks in a server rack diagram
Training requires constant gradient communication between GPUs, and slow interconnects can make communication time dominate over compute time
Interconnect topology only matters for single-GPU training
GPUs never need to communicate with each other during training
questions.explain: Multi-GPU training requires gradients to be exchanged and averaged across GPUs after every backward pass. If that communication is slow, it can dominate total training time regardless of how fast each individual GPU computes.
